own_solution.law: Momentum conservation in a perfectly inelastic collision; KE lost = (1/2) mu v_rel^2
assumptions: isolated two-particle system on frictionless ice

defect_reasons.other: T081E does not say whether the stated 4 m/s holds after the bag is picked up; the authors' wiring keeps v1 = 4 m/s with mass m1+q (the natural reading of the present-tense description), but picking up a bag at rest from the ice would by momentum conservation lower the speed to 3.33 m/s and give 369.39 J.

notes: Certified answers verified: q=3.5: mu=63.5*75/138.5=34.386, loss=429.83 J; q=12: 5400/147=36.735, 459.18 J; q=15: 37.5, 468.75 J; base 416.67 J. Minimal pairs T3B70/T90B7 (coach vs east skater) and T3DB2/T081E (earlier outing vs before this collision) both state 12 kg and differ only in attachment. Numeral-free twins consistent. Agrees with pass 1.
